subcategoria: La Casa de las Tres Lunas

poema.texto:
En una noche de luna pura y tranquila,
En la Casa de las Tres Lunas se reveló,
Un enigma misterioso, que allí convulsa,
Un secreto antiguo al mundo se mostró.

El cielo de estrellas brillaba claro y blanco,
Los gatos de la noche en el pueblo se escuchaban,
Y los arbustos a su alrededor, se movían lento,
Su murmullo susurrando las sombras del día anunciaba.

Una luz aparició, que brotó de la casa vieja,
El encantamiento del aire comenzó entonces,
Ese poder misterioso, que en el silencio se decía,
Un secreto profundo, que no se había escuchado.

Un resplandor de azul brillaba en las nubes oscuras,
Como un signo divino del universo,
El tiempo se detuvo, como si fuera un acto,
De una tragedia que ya estaba desarrollándose.

Los tres lunares que brindaban su luz en el cielo,
Se transformaron en figuras antiguas y bellas,
Pero en ese momento, los árboles se vuelven pálidos,
Y la sangre de las personas comenzó a congelar.

Los ojos de las mujeres se volvieron como las piedras,
Y los hombres estaban llorando sin llanto,
Se sentían mal en su alma, pero no podían decir por qué,
El secreto que había surgido, estaba destruyendo.

Suddenly the three lunar ladies began to speak in unison,
Their voices echoing through the air,
Their words seemed to carry the weight of a million suns,
A tale of love and betrayal that none could bear.

In the heart of the village, a man stood tall and proud,
His eyes filled with fear and sorrow,
He knew the secret they spoke, was his alone,
And with it came a burden he couldn't borrow.

The tale unfolded, as the moonlight danced and shone,
Of a love that had blossomed years ago,
Between the man and one of the three,
A union forbidden by fate, as they were told to go.

But the love they shared, could not be denied,
And so they ran away from their world,
They built a home in the heart of the forest,
Where their love story would forever unfold.

Years passed and the man aged with grace,
While the three remained ageless and beautiful,
But as fate would have it, the truth came to light,
And the man was banished from his paradise.

Now, on this night, he returned to reclaim his love,
But as he approached the house of the ladies,
He saw them standing together, side by side,
Their eyes filled with sorrow, but no malice or anger.

"Why have you come?" one of them asked, her voice trembling with pain,
"To take me from my home and my sisters?" she pleaded,
"No, my love," he replied, "I never meant to cause you such pain,
But I cannot bear to live without you by my side."

In that moment, the air grew thick with tears,
As they clung to each other in a silent embrace,
Their hearts pounding like drums, echoing their fears,
And time seemed to stand still as they kissed and gave grace.

But as their lips touched, the world around them shattered,
The three lunar ladies transformed once more,
The man screamed as he watched his love fade away,
And the forest closed in around him, never to be explored.

Now, on this night, the story is told again,
Of a love that was lost and a curse that followed,
A tale of passion and tragedy, that will never end,
And the House of the Three Lunas, will always stand as a monument to their story, forever echoing through the ages.
